method.protocol: static 0 K E(V) scan, 15 isotropic strains of the 8-atom cubic diamond cell, spans +-2% and +-5%, Birch-Murnaghan and Vinet fits

payload.note: PREMISE: well posed. The static equilibrium lattice constant of a perfect crystal comes straight out of an E(V) fit. An 8-atom cubic cell is enough for a perfect diamond lattice, and no ensemble or run length applies. REPRODUCTION: my own script (the worker's /work/eos_results.json and script were not in my workspace) with the same MACE-MP-0 medium float64 model gave a = 5.4556 A (+-2%, BM and Vinet) and 5.4560-5.4562 A (+-5%), B0 = 74.6 GPa, residual stress 0.022 GPa. That matches the worker's 5.456 A, 74.5 GPa and 0.024 GPa. SECOND MLIP: MACE-MPA-0 medium, trained on more data (MPtrj+sAlex), gave a = 5.4659-5.4673 A (B0 about 86-89 GPa). MACE-MP-0 small gave 5.461-5.464 A. All three MACE models fall within 5.456-5.467 A, a spread of about 0.01 A, well inside the worker's +-0.03 A. Caveat: all three are MACE models fit to PBE-level data, so they are not fully independent. LITERATURE ANCHOR: a PAW PBE value for Si of 5.467 A against an experimental 5.430 A is listed in arXiv:2010.13050 ('Semiconductor Physics: A Density Functional Journey'). MACE-MP-0 medium is therefore about 0.01 A below its PBE parent, and MPA-0 essentially reproduces it. The worker's experimental reference (CODATA 2018, 5.431020511 A at 22.5 C) is correct. The +0.46% deviation is the usual PBE overestimate; it is not a fitting error. The tier1 calibration file has no silicon record, so it was not used. CAVEATS (agree with the worker): this is a static-lattice value with no zero-point or thermal expansion, while experiment includes both. The +-0.03 A uncertainty is a fair statement of model/functional systematic error. Verdict: agree, with 5.456 A as the MACE-MP-0 static-lattice PBE-level prediction. A value from the newer MACE-MPA-0 model would be about 5.466 A.
